citeAs: Grigor Bezirganyan, Sana Sellami, Laure Berti-Équille, and Sébastien Fournier. 2025. LUMA: A Benchmark Dataset for Learning from Uncertain and Multimodal Data. In Proceedings of the 48th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval (SIGIR '25), July 13–18, 2025, Padua, Italy. ACM, New York, NY, USA. https://doi.org/10.1145/3726302.3730302
creator: Grigor Bezirganyan, Sana Sellami, Laure Berti-Équille, Sébastien Fournier (Aix Marseille Univ, CNRS, LIS; IRD, ESPACE-DEV)
description: LUMA (Learning from Uncertain and Multimodal data) is a multimodal benchmark dataset featuring audio, image, and textual data from 50 classes, specifically designed for learning from uncertain data. It includes 101,000 images, 135,096 speech audio recordings, and 62,875 text passages (~3 GB), extending CIFAR-10/100 with audio samples from three corpora and text generated using Gemma-7B LLM. The dataset enables controlled injection of varying types and degrees of uncertainty, and is accompanied by a Python package for generating variants with controllable noise, diversity, and out-of-distribution samples.
name: LUMA
rai:annotatorDemographics: 17 annotators who were colleagues (M.Sc. and PhD students, and professors) with advanced to fluent English knowledge
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: 71.61% annotation agreement was achieved. Samples where both annotators confirmed validity were accepted (5,027 samples). Samples with conflicting annotations were rejected.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Audio samples that failed automatic validation (via Whisper Large V3 transcription) were sent for manual validation. Annotators were shown the audio sample and asked "Is the audio saying the word below? (An extra 's' or 'es' in the pronunciation is okay.)" with Yes/No options. Only samples where both annotators confirmed validity were accepted; conflicting annotations were rejected.
rai:dataBiases: Gender bias was identified in LLM-generated text for classes "man", "woman", "boy", and "girl". The Gemma model detected gender, racial, religious, and cultural biases in generated texts. Prompts were reconstructed for these 4 classes to reduce bias, but significant bias still exists. The dataset may also contain factual inaccuracies due to LLM generation.
rai:dataCollection: Images were sourced from CIFAR-10/100 datasets (with some EDM diffusion-generated images for diversity). Audio samples were extracted from three corpora: The Spoken Wikipedia, LibriSpeech, and Mozilla Common Voice, plus 73 voluntary recordings from colleagues. Text passages were generated using the Gemma-7B Instruct LLM with 13 different prompts per class label.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images: CIFAR-10/100 (32x32 images) and EDM diffusion-generated images. Audio: The Spoken Wikipedia corpus, LibriSpeech corpus (1,000 hours of English speech from audiobooks), and Mozilla Common Voice (crowdsourced open-source voice recordings), plus 73 voluntary colleague recordings. Text: LLM-generated passages using Gemma-7B Instruct.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, User-generated content data, Others
rai:dataLimitations: Since textual data was generated using an LLM, the dataset may contain factual inaccuracies or biases. LUMA shall not be used as a source of knowledge or information. Audio samples from forced alignments may contain misaligned segments introducing additional noise. Voluntary audio contributions may include very noisy samples or samples with strong accents.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The Python package supports: (1) Data diversity control via inverse-distance-weighted sampling using deep features (Wav2Vec for audio, BERT for text, VGG-11 for images); (2) Sample noise injection — background noise from ESC-50 for audio, nlpaug-based noise (keyboard, OCR, random character, antonym, random word, spelling, back-translation) for text, and 15 image perturbations (Gaussian noise, shot noise, blur types, weather effects, etc.); (3) Label noise injection by reassigning labels to semantically closest class; (4) OOD sample injection from held-out classes.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio: Force-aligned alignments generated with Montreal Forced Aligner for LibriSpeech and Mozilla Common Voice; audio segments extracted by matching class labels (including plural forms); automatic validation via Whisper Large V3 transcription; manual validation via Label Studio for borderline cases; voluntary recordings were anonymized and trimmed. Text: Generated texts validated by masking label occurrences and re-classifying with Gemma-7B; biased texts filtered out; prompts reconstructed for 4 gender-sensitive classes. Images: 42 classes selected with ≥600 samples; 8 classes with <600 samples used as OOD.
rai:dataSocialImpact: LUMA is intended to promote the development of trustworthy and robust multimodal deep learning approaches for safety-critical applications such as healthcare and autonomous driving. The dataset enables benchmarking of uncertainty quantification methods, which is essential for deploying reliable AI in high-stakes domains.
rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking multimodal uncertainty quantification methods; evaluating robustness of multimodal deep learning models to noise; studying aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty in multimodal settings; out-of-distribution detection research; development of trustworthy AI for safety-critical applications.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: OpenAI Whisper Large V3 (for automatic audio transcription and validation); Gemma-7B Instruct (for text generation and bias detection); Montreal Forced Aligner (for word-level alignment of LibriSpeech and Mozilla Common Voice audio)
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: 73 voluntary audio recordings from colleagues were anonymized before inclusion in the dataset.

null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper does not explicitly discuss missing data handling beyond the audio validation/filtering process, which is covered under preprocessing.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific timeframe or date range for data collection is mentioned in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol is described; missing/invalid samples are filtered out rather than imputed.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No explicit versioning, update cadence, or maintenance plan is described beyond a general statement about future extensions.

evidence.name: We propose LUMA, a unique multimodal dataset, featuring audio, image, and textual data from 50 classes, specifically designed for learning from uncertain data.
evidence.description: The dataset includes 101,000 images, 135,096 speech audio recordings, and 62,875 text passages, amounting to approximately 3 GB of data. Each modality is independently sourced, reflecting real-world conditions where data is often collected under different conditions and times.
evidence.creator: Grigor Bezirganyan, Sana Sellami, Laure Berti-Équille, and Sébastien Fournier. 2025. LUMA: A Benchmark Dataset for Learning from Uncertain and Multimodal Data.

evidence.inLanguage: The LibriSpeech dataset is a corpus of 1,000 hours of English speech, derived from audiobooks from the LibriVox project

evidence.isLiveDataset: The dataset can be easily extended with additional modalities and augmented with more data samples. In the future, we plan to include dependent modalities
evidence.rai:annotationsPerItem: In total, we collected 2 annotations per sample, from 17 annotators.
evidence.rai:annotatorDemographics: We asked our colleagues (M.Sc. and PhD students, and professors) with advanced to fluent English knowledge to annotate the samples. In total, we collected 2 annotations per sample, from 17 annotators.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: We got 71.61% annotation agreement and accepted 5,027 samples, where both annotators confirmed the validity of the sample. Samples with conflicting annotations were rejected.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: We opted for Label Studio to build the labeling interface. The interface provided the audio sample, with the prompt "Is the audio saying the word below? (An extra 's' or 'es' in the pronunciation is okay.)" and answer options of "Yes" or "No".
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The interface provided the audio sample, with the prompt "Is the audio saying the word below? (An extra 's' or 'es' in the pronunciation is okay.)" and answer options of "Yes" or "No". We asked our colleagues (M.Sc. and PhD students, and professors) with advanced to fluent English knowledge to annotate the samples.
evidence.rai:dataBiases: Particularly, we noticed a lots of gender bias for classes "man", "woman", "boy" and "girl". To find the proportion of the biased data, we asked the Gemma model to find out if the given text contains gender, racial, religious, or cultural biases.
evidence.rai:dataCollection: We compiled the images from the CIFAR 10/100 dataset, extracted, validated, and associated audio samples corresponding to the CIFAR image class labels from three diverse audio corpora, and generated the text modality based on the class labels using the Gemma-7B Instruct Large Language Model (LLM).
evidence.rai:dataCollectionRawData: For audio modality, the diversity of accent in the pronunciation was an important factor to consider, and we collected samples, where different people would pronounce the corresponding class label of CIFAR 10/100 images. For this task, we used three audio/text parallel corpora and extracted the desired audio segments. More specifically, we used The Spoken Wikipedia, LibriSpeech, and Mozilla Common Voice corpora.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionType: We compiled the images from the CIFAR 10/100 dataset, extracted, validated, and associated audio samples corresponding to the CIFAR image class labels from three diverse audio corpora, and generated the text modality based on the class labels using the Gemma-7B Instruct Large Language Model (LLM).
evidence.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The automatic validation was achieved with the OpenAI's Whisper Large V3 model for audio transcription, and transcribed the extracted audio samples. If the transcription corresponded to the class label (or its plural form), then we considered the sample as valid. Otherwise, the sample was sent for manual validation.
evidence.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: We prioritized flexibility, offering multiple options for controlling uncertainty through adjustable parameters such as data diversity, sample-level noise, label corruption, and the injection of out-of-distribution (OOD) samples.
evidence.rai:dataLimitations: Since textual data was generated using an LLM, we recognize that the dataset may contain factual inaccuracies, or biases, but our aim is to offer a benchmark to study uncertainty quantification in multimodal classification settings. LUMA shall not be used as a source of knowledge or information.
evidence.rai:dataSocialImpact: We anticipate that the LUMA dataset will help the research community to design more trustworthy and robust machine learning approaches for safety critical applications.
evidence.rai:dataUseCases: This comprehensive dataset and its tools are intended to promote and support the development, evaluation, and benchmarking of trustworthy and robust multimodal deep learning approaches.
evidence.rai:machineAnnotationTools: The automatic validation was achieved with the OpenAI's Whisper Large V3 model for audio transcription, and transcribed the extracted audio samples. If the transcription corresponded to the class label (or its plural form), then we considered the sample as valid.
evidence.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: 73 additional recordings of pronunciations belonging to 4 classes ("roses", "telephone", "whale", "wolf") were voluntarily contributed by our colleagues, which were anonymized, trimmed, and added to the dataset.
